newsitem.title: USA: USDA - Sun-Diamond barred from purchase programs.
newsitem.headline: USDA - Sun-Diamond barred from purchase programs.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Friday that Sun-Diamond Growers of California would be excluded from participating in any federal purchase programs and proposed it be debarred for three years.

"USDA is taking this action because of Sun-Diamond's recent federal court conviction for acts that seriously question the cooperative's business integrity or honesty," Robert Keeney of USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service said in a statement.
"This action is being taken to protect the interests of the federal government," Keeney said.
USDA also barred former Sun-Diamond vice-president Richard Douglas and lobbyst James Lake from federal purchase programs.

Sun Diamond, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, was convicted last month in a federal court on eight criminal counts that included illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994 and illegal campaign contributions to Espy's brother Henry.
The charges arose out of the government's two-year special investigation of the former Agriculture Secretary.
USDA said a proposed debarment by one federal agency automatically excludes a firm or individual from participating as a contractor or subcontractor throughout the executive branch.
It said Sun-Diamond, Douglas and Lake have 30 days from the date of debarment notification to appeal.
USDA said it would "continue reviewing official documents pertaining to Sun-Diamond's federal court conviction to determine what additional actions will be taken."
